          Arsenal Have Hit Their First Bump in the Road – Here’s Why They Should Bounce Back
        
      
                          
                      Oct 9, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Yash Thakur / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
A heavy defeat to Brighton was followed by injuries to some key players during the international break, but Arsenal have spent years building a squad capable of absorbing such setbacks. Now it‘s time for their depth to shine through.
It’s been a long three weeks for Arsenal fans. Three weeks to stew over their club’s worst result, and arguably poorest performance, in a very long time.

Mikel Arteta’s side were completely blown away by Brighton on Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 Premier League season. They lost 3-0 on the south coast, unable to cope with the intensity and relentlessness of Brighton’s press.
It was Arsenal’s biggest defeat in any competition for more than three years. The last time they lost a game by three or more goals was also against Brighton, back in a 3-0 home defeat in May 2023.
Then came the international break and the dreaded injuries that can accompany it.

Kai Havertz was forced off in Germany’s first game against the Netherlands with a suspected hamstring injury. Christos Tzolis then suffered the same fate against the same opposition for Greece last week. Both had started the season excellently for Arsenal; they could each now miss multiple weeks of action.

Ezri Konsa, who has slotted in superbly at the heart of the defence amid William Saliba’s continued absence, also had to withdraw early from England’s Nations League squad after sustaining a knock in training.
Suddenly, three members of Arsenal’s first-choice starting XI are doubts for this weekend. In the cases of Havertz and Tzolis, their absences could stretch well beyond that.

Heading into MD5, it felt like there was no stopping the Gunners. They had won each of their first four Premier League games, as well as three more in other competitions, and few of their opponents had caused them any real problems. Then Brighton completely outplayed them, and they have now lost several first-choice players to injury.

But if any side has the resilience and squad depth to handle setbacks like these – and it's worth saying that Arsenal are hardly the only team to have suffered injuries during the international break – it's this one. Arteta will not be overly worried, and neither should the fans be.

The very fact the Brighton game was Arsenal’s heaviest defeat in more than three years shows just how rare it is for Arteta's men to have an off day. It was only the second time in their last 158 matches in all competitions that they had conceded three goals. It's also their only defeat in their last 16 games in all competitions.
This is a side who have been consistently dominant for more than 12 months, and defensively dominant for even longer.

Arsenal have typically responded well to setbacks, too. Since the start of 2024, they've lost back-to-back Premier League games just once, against Bournemouth and Manchester City in April this year. Saturday’s meeting with Leeds will be their 100th league game since the beginning of that year.
For context, City have suffered consecutive league defeats on three separate occasions over the same period.

There is every chance, then, that Arsenal bounce back strongly when the action returns. Leeds have done well this season and are one of only five unbeaten teams, but Arsenal have an excellent record against them.

The Gunners have won nine of the two teams' last 10 Premier League meetings (D1), including the last seven by an aggregate score of 24-5. Last season, they won 5-0 at the Emirates and 4-0 at Elland Road.
That home meeting saw Viktor Gyökeres score the first goals of his Arsenal career, and he has netted more Premier League goals against Leeds (3) than any other opponent.

For all the harm the international break has done to Arsenal's squad, the former Sporting CP striker is one player returning from a very productive few games, scoring in all four of Sweden’s Nations League matches. With Havertz sidelined, Gyökeres is his natural replacement.

The Swede has unfortunately become something of a figure of amusement among rival fans, having failed to fully live up to the lofty expectations that came with his big-money move to north London. While he has hardly been a slam-dunk signing, he remains a capable alternative to Havertz, is in good form, and should be able to lead the line effectively in upcoming fixtures against Leeds, Lille and Nottingham Forest.

It's also worth remembering what he achieved last season. Gyökeres became the first player to score 20 or more goals in all competitions during his debut Arsenal season since Alexis Sánchez hit 25 in 2014-15. The only other player to do so for the club in the Premier League era is Thierry Henry, who scored 26 in 1999-2000. However you spin it, his goals undoubtedly helped Arsenal win the Premier League and reach the Champions League final.
